blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — peripheral nerve block safety
stem: After orthopedic surgery, a client has temporary numbness and weakness in one leg from a peripheral nerve block. Which teaching by the nurse is most appropriate?

options.A: Do not stand, walk, or place pressure on the affected leg until the care team confirms it is safe; protect the numb limb until sensation and motor control adequately return.
options.B: Bear full weight on the affected leg as soon as pain is absent because lack of pain confirms that strength, balance, and protective sensation are fully restored.
options.C: Apply sustained pressure to the numb area to test whether sensation is returning because pressure testing is a safe way to judge readiness for walking after a nerve block.
options.D: Remove protective devices from the blocked limb because temporary numbness prevents pressure injury and reduces the need for assistance with standing or transfers.

rationale: Current ASRA Pain Medicine patient guidance explains that regional blocks can cause temporary numbness, heaviness, weakness, incomplete muscle control, difficulty with weight bearing, and fall risk. Patients should check with the physician or nurse before using the affected extremity for standing or other motor tasks and should not put pressure on an extremity that remains numb. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Protect an extremity affected by a peripheral nerve block by avoiding unapproved weight bearing or pressure until sensation and motor control have returned adequately.
source_organization: American Society of Regional Anesthesia and Pain Medicine (ASRA Pain Medicine)
source_document_title: Pain Relief After Surgery; Regional Anesthesia for Surgery

source_locator: Pain Relief After Surgery §4 and §6: local anesthetics can cause numbness/heaviness, difficulty weight bearing, fall risk, temporary weakness and incomplete muscle control; check with clinician before standing/motor tasks and do not put pressure on a numb extremity. Regional Anesthesia for Surgery: blocked leg may have weight-bearing difficulty and fall precautions are required.
source_claim_supported: Regional blocks can temporarily impair sensation and motor control; weight bearing and pressure on the numb extremity should be avoided until safe use is confirmed.
